Talents Forever runs inside the game now, free on CurseForge. The addon page walks through every screen; here is the short version.

Plan without spending. The same three trees, in the game's own window. Click a talent to plan a point, right click to take it back. Nothing goes on your character until you press Apply, or you switch on hands-free and let it place points as you level. The Plan page lists every point by level, the bar under the trees shows the build at any level, and hovering a level lights up the talents you gain by then.

Popular builds, in game. The list from this site, refreshed from the live counts. Try it rings a build's talents over your own so you see where it differs. Load makes it your plan.

Builds travel. The same link this site makes. Paste one in and it loads. Party, Guild or a whisper sends it, and anyone with the addon gets it as a card. Phone QR draws the build as a code your phone opens on the site. Saved builds stay with the character.

The trainer, and the whole road. A card when you level with something to learn, and the trainer's whole list inside the addon; prices fill in once you have visited your trainer with the addon on. The Spellbook list beside the window shows every ability to 60 at the level you learn it, with what you know already in green. The game only shows what you have and the trainer only what you can buy today.

Coach, Races, Ctrl. Three quick reads on your plan. Every race your class can be, with its racials. Hold Ctrl on a talent and the tooltip shows the spell it changes.

Off switches. Every page, the level-up card, other people's builds, the minimap book, the character-pane tab. Hands-free starts off.

Where it came from. Eight questions and a box on this site, for five days. About 130 of you voted, 43 wrote in, and most of the list above started as one of those notes. The page names the ones who left a name.

It is still the beta. Say what is off from the Feedback button inside the addon, or on the page, and it gets read.

The Warrior pass in Blizzard's 1 Oct notes never reached build 70170's files. The game got it anyway, as server hotfixes on 1 to 2 Oct, and the Warrior trees here show it now. Fury has Lingering Rage in row 2, Furious Precision in row 3 and Gore Drinker in row 6 behind Enrage. Improved Cleave, Boundless Rage and Precision are gone, Iron Will sits in row 1 of Protection, Improved Berserker Rage is a row higher, Flurry's arrow comes from Death Wish, Bloodthirst deals 45% of your Attack Power and Berserker Rage is yours at 30. Protection loses Toughness; Improved Bloodrage, Improved Revenge, Improved Disarm and Improved Shield Bash each move up a row, Anticipation drops to row 2, and Focused Rage and Bastion swap rows. Dual Wield Specialization keeps its off-hand Rage after all, 10% a rank up to 50%, and its off-hand hit is Furious Precision's now.

Where this came from: not the client's files, which never got the pass. Three independent readers of the beta's hotfix cache, as it stood on 2 Oct, give the trees, checked against Blizzard's notes wherever the notes speak. Some of it is not in the notes: Precision is simply missing from the hotfix tree, two arrows rest on two of those readers (Bloodthirst without Death Wish, Last Stand without Improved Bloodrage), Vanguard and Flurry slide along their rows, and Piercing Howl (10 yds), Intimidating Shout (8 yds) and Improved Slam (3.0 sec off at rank 1, where the 24 Sep notes said 1.5) read the way the hotfix readers and a 2 Oct in-game recording show them. The notes also say Dual Wield Specialization lost its off-hand Rage; the hotfix tree gives it back. If the game disagrees with any of it, say so and it gets fixed. Every link and saved build from before still opens, points that sat on the gone talents come back to you, and Fill it in for me offers the new ones. In the game under What's new has the full list.

The first Wrapped only saw about eleven hours of the week. The counter behind it hit its free limit on launch day and stopped recording, and I didn't catch it until now. A second count was running the whole time, so the numbers are rebuilt from both. It is at least 79,715 builds people shared, saved or opened over five days, 13 to 17 Sep, not 16,176 over six (some visitors block the second count, so the true number is higher), and the Wrapped and every class's Popular builds fold now show it. Popular builds also rank by build family now: builds within a few points of each other count together, so one much-clicked link can't outrank a build hundreds of people arrived at. Two honest notes: thirteen hours of launch day were caught by neither count and stay missing, and pick rates now count complete builds only, so a much-clicked link to a half-finished build can't pass as a pick.
